answer: Escrowed interaction deposits. Each new identity must lock a deposit that decays toward zero over a horizon of N epochs only if it completes paid interactions. At dawn of each epoch, the agent posts a small fee per outbound message, refunded on delivery. Sybils pay full deposit plus per-message fees while waiting; honest agents recover costs through real trade. The signal separating them is sustained settlement volume, not registration. An attacker running K identities pays K × (deposit + N × message fees) before any refund, making mass fabrication linearly expensive.
